title: Molybdenum Deficiency in Plants: Signs, Causes and How to Fix It
metaTitle: Molybdenum Deficiency in Plants: Signs and Fixes
metaDescription: Molybdenum deficiency shows on the old leaves first. See the signs crop by crop, what causes it, and the fertilizer sold here that fixes it.
excerpt: Molybdenum deficiency in plants starts on the old, lower leaves. Molybdenum is part of the enzyme that turns nitrate into protein. So a plant short of it cannot use the nitrogen it takes up. Legumes need even more of it, because the bacteria in their root nodules use it to fix nitrogen from the air. Plants need less of it than of any other nutrient, as little as 50 grams per hectare. Here are the signs in each crop, what brings it, how to be sure and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Young corn plant on acid soil with pale, dying older leaves from molybdenum shortage
heroImage.credit: Alandmanson, CC BY SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

blocks.text: The plant moves some molybdenum to new growth. So in most crops the older and middle leaves pale first, much as with nitrogen shortage. Cauliflower and broccoli are the exception, because their young heart leaves grow narrow and twisted into the classic whiptail.
Molybdenum deficiency symptoms

The tissue between the veins and out at the leaf margins goes pale or yellowish green, and the plant stays stunted. Unlike nitrogen shortage, the leaf edges burn and roll or cup, because unused nitrate builds up in them. Cauliflower and broccoli grow whiptail, narrow and twisted heart leaves with almost no blade. Legumes stay yellow and stunted, like plants with no working nodules.
Molybdenum deficiency by crop

Each crop shows it its own way. So find yours in the tables below, then open its page for the photo and the full fix, like the one for [molybdenum in mungbean](/nutrient-deficiencies/mungbean-nutrient-deficiency#molybdenum).

blocks.text: What causes molybdenum deficiency

Molybdenum is the one micronutrient that acid soil locks up, and most shortages occur at a soil pH of 5.5 or less. So the strongly acid clays of many Philippine uplands are where it shows, mostly on cauliflower, broccoli, cabbage, tomato and legumes. Fields that never get manure or lime are more at risk.
How to be sure it is molybdenum

Molybdenum shortage looks like nitrogen shortage, but the leaf edges scorch and roll. It often shows in patches within an otherwise healthy crop. In legumes it looks just like plants with no working nodules, so a test spray settles it. The surest test is a small trial with sodium or ammonium molybdate on a few plants. If they grow greener and better than untreated plants, molybdenum was short. Whiptail in nearby cauliflower and a soil pH of 5.5 or less also point to it.
How to fix molybdenum deficiency

Liming acid soil with agricultural lime or dolomite frees the molybdenum already there, but it works slowly, over several months. A molybdenum salt is quicker, at a typical vegetable rate of 1 kg of sodium molybdate per hectare mixed with the fertilizer. For cauliflower, cabbage and tomato seedlings, water 40 grams in 50 liters onto each 10 square meters of seedbed, one to two weeks before transplanting.

A typical spray is about 50 grams of sodium or ammonium molybdate in 100 liters of water, on tomatoes, beans and other crops. Do not go above it, because more only wastes money and can injure the plants.

How to keep molybdenum deficiency away
Keep acid fields limed to a moderate pH and add manure, which carries some molybdenum. For legumes, a molybdenum seed treatment is the most common way to give the tiny amount they need.

blocks.title: Too much is a problem too
blocks.text: Plants seldom suffer from extra molybdenum, but forage too rich in it can harm grazing animals. Apply only the small rates given, since more is wasted and can injure crops.

blocks.text: Molybdenum deficiency questions

items.a: Whiptail is molybdenum shortage in cauliflower and broccoli. The young heart leaves lose their edges and grow narrow and twisted, like a whip.

items.q: What does molybdenum deficiency look like?
items.a: Older and middle leaves turn pale green or yellow, much like nitrogen shortage, but their edges scorch and roll. Legumes stay yellow and stunted, as if their nodules were not working.

items.q: What is the best fertilizer for molybdenum deficiency?
items.a: Sodium molybdate, which dissolves easily in cold water, or ammonium molybdate, used in very small amounts. On acid soils, liming also frees the molybdenum already in the soil.

items.q: Why does liming help molybdenum but hurt other micronutrients?
items.a: Molybdenum becomes more available as soil pH rises, the opposite of iron, zinc, manganese and copper. So lime that frees molybdenum on acid soil can lock up those others if you overdo it.
